tests.title: runs against a reference built from commit 946fcce0 with --disable-x86asm
matches native framecrc for delay, decay, speed and gain sweeps over every native sample format, 1-3 channels at 8000 and 44100 Hz
writes native-identical WAV, raw and framecrc output from raw and WAV input with output -ss, -t and -frames:a, and composes with volume
does not depend on frame grouping: asetnsamples=n=1/7/29/50:p=0 before aphaser matches native and ungrouped output byte for byte
matches native on every platform for integer input with binary-fraction gains at power-of-two modulation lengths, full-scale s32 on the clipping bound included
refuses sinusoidal modulation, gains past the clipping bound, delays that round to zero and enable before output, with native status for each case
parses named and positional options, type=t, and refuses sinusoidal, enable, expressions, clipping gains and out-of-range values with exact messages
computes buffer lengths and the triangle table from config_output and ff_generate_wave_table, refusing delays that round to zero
negotiates the native list, plans unchanged counts and packet sections, and reserves one frame plus the delay rings
refuses rates whose delay rounds to zero in constraint(), before any frame, and accepts every channel count and layout
matches the C transcription in every kernel format, packed and planar, across 1/7/29/50-sample splits, keeping timestamps and owning output
keeps every integer output at the s32 and s16 extremes in range when the gains sit exactly on the clipping bound
converts u8 input to s16, enforces allocation and format limits, refuses non-finite samples and stops on abort

detail: 868 framecrc (Linux x64 gate): u8/s16/s32/f32/f64 raw input x 8000/44100 Hz x 1-3 channels x 14 chains (9 sweeps of delay 0.1-5, decay 0-0.99, speed 0.1-2 and gains on/inside the bound; aformat=s16p/s32p/fltp/dblp before; asetnsamples=7 before) x input codec/pcm_s16le/(stereo) pcm_f64le, -cpuflags 0
196 files (Linux x64 gate): s16/f32 raw and WAV input, 3 chains, output -ss/-t/-frames:a/-ss+-t, WAV/raw/framecrc; aphaser,volume=0.5 on u8 and f32 input
20 raw outputs (Linux x64 gate) for asetnsamples=n=1/7/29/50:p=0 grouping, plus 16 checks that native grouped output equals ungrouped output
74 framecrc on every platform: u8/s16/s32/full-scale s32 at 8192 Hz with exact binary-fraction gains on the clipping bound and power-of-two table lengths, 2 empty inputs

15 native exit statuses: type=s (3 spellings) and 4 gains past the bound (native 0), 3 delays rounding to zero (native 256-EINVAL), enable= x2, delay=6, type=x (native fails), aphaser,volume=0.5 on s16 (native 0); all refused here before output

unsupported: gains past native out_gain clipping condition in_gain/(1-decay) > 1/out_gain (native warns and, for integer kernels, converts out of range with undefined behaviour)
option expressions, exponents, SI suffixes, signs and escaping
FLAC input (refused before decoding; flacInput not declared)
automatic sample-rate conversion around the step
aphaser,volume=... on s16/s32/dbl input (native merges to flt; refused by the negotiation guard)

proposedContracts.name: runs against a reference built from commit 946fcce0 with --disable-x86asm
matches native framecrc for delay, decay, speed and gain sweeps over every native sample format, 1-3 channels at 8000 and 44100 Hz
writes native-identical WAV, raw and framecrc output from raw and WAV input with output -ss, -t and -frames:a, and composes with volume
does not depend on frame grouping: asetnsamples=n=1/7/29/50:p=0 before aphaser matches native and ungrouped output byte for byte
matches native on every platform for integer input with binary-fraction gains at power-of-two modulation lengths, full-scale s32 on the clipping bound included
refuses sinusoidal modulation, gains past the clipping bound, delays that round to zero and enable before output, with native status for each case
parses named and positional options, type=t, and refuses sinusoidal, enable, expressions, clipping gains and out-of-range values with exact messages
computes buffer lengths and the triangle table from config_output and ff_generate_wave_table, refusing delays that round to zero
negotiates the native list, plans unchanged counts and packet sections, and reserves one frame plus the delay rings
refuses rates whose delay rounds to zero in constraint(), before any frame, and accepts every channel count and layout
matches the C transcription in every kernel format, packed and planar, across 1/7/29/50-sample splits, keeping timestamps and owning output
keeps every integer output at the s32 and s16 extremes in range when the gains sit exactly on the clipping bound
converts u8 input to s16, enforces allocation and format limits, refuses non-finite samples and stops on abort

notes: formats() is the native [dbl, dblp, flt, fltp, s32, s32p, s16, s16p]; no negotiate/nativeFormats/flacInput; not transparent.

The clipping-bound proof (docs/contributing/aphaser.md) shows native's double-evaluated condition keeps every s32/s16 output within (-2^31-1, 2^31) with a margin above 1-2^-14 under double rounding, so the bound is not tightened; a unit test drives full-scale s32/s16 input on the bound.

The triangle table is computed per sample in the same double operations instead of being held; checked against a transcription of ff_generate_wave_table. reserve() declares 1 frame plus delay_buffer_length*channels*8 state bytes.

Float-sensitive cases (any non-exact gain, float or integer kernel) are gated to linux-x64 as a precaution; no macOS difference was measured (Linux-only sandbox). The exact-gain integer test at 8192 Hz runs everywhere.
A one-off mutation of the modulation position made four differential tests fail.

Setup: Node 24.22.3 from /opt/node24 (sandbox default was 22, which bootstrap refuses). Bootstrap (npm, submodule, reference) 190 s, reference build 175 s; baseline typecheck+lint+boundaries 56 s; baseline registry unit tests 4 s (26 passed). aphaser unit file ~10 s; differential file 23 s with --maxWorkers=1.
The sandbox ffmpeg differs from the linux-x64 pin (accepted with --allow-unpinned-reference); the tests pin no binary digest.
